title: Unreal time
subtitle: Hypothetical past forms, wishes, it's time, would rather, as if / as though

items: Sometimes we use the past simple and past continuous to refer to the present, the future or a general situation.
Sometimes we use the past perfect simple and past perfect continuous to refer to a hypothetical past that did not actually happen.

blocks.text: After **I** and **he/she/it**, there is a choice of **was** or **were**. Both **was** and **were** are common in informal English, but **were** is sometimes more appropriate in formal, written English and is always used in **If I were you …**
blocks.note: I wish I **was** rich. · I wish I **were** rich.

rows.use: Hypothetical or unlikely current, future or general conditions
rows.example: I wouldn't accept a job unless I **was** absolutely sure about the salary. · If you **were travelling** to Russia, would you get roubles before you left?
If I **had known**, I would have taken some cash with me. · If I **had been running** the bank, I would have given you an overdraft!

rows.use: Hypothetical or unlikely current, future or general situations
rows.example: Supposing you **were given** ten million euros, what would you spend it on? · What if you **were walking** down the street and you suddenly found a wallet?
Suppose you **had won** the lottery last night. What would you have done? · Imagine you'd **been working** there for 40 years. What kind of pension would you have got?

blocks.text: We can also use a present tense instead of past simple or past continuous after these words. This indicates that the situation is more likely to happen.
blocks.note: Supposing you **become** a millionaire, how will it change your life? (more likely) · Supposing you **became** a millionaire, how would it change your life? (less likely)

rows.use: Current, future or general untrue, hypothetical comparisons
rows.example: She acts **as if/though she was** a millionaire. · Colin acts **as if/though he were making** a million pounds a month.
Tony looks **as if/though someone had just handed** him a million euros. · It's almost **as if/though they'd been working** for free.

blocks.text: When the verb before **as if/though** is in a present or present perfect tense, we only use a past tense for comparisons that we know aren't true. When the comparison is possible, we use a present or present perfect tense after **as if/though**.
blocks.note: She behaves **as if she were** wealthy. (= She's not really wealthy.) · She looks **as if she's** really wealthy. (= It's very possible that she is wealthy.)

blocks.text: When the verb before **as if/though** is in a past tense, we use a past tense after **as if/though** for comparisons that are either true or hypothetical.
blocks.note: She **looked as if she was** really wealthy but I knew she wasn't / so maybe she was.

rows.use: To make questions and requests more polite
rows.example: How much money **did you want** to spend, madam? · I **was wondering** whether you might be able to give me some advice.

rows.use: To suggest that something should be done now or in the immediate future
rows.example: It's (high/about) time I **got** a mortgage. · It's (high/about) time we **were leaving**.

blocks.text: With **it's (high/about) time**, there is often no real difference in meaning between past simple and past continuous.
blocks.note: It's time I **went** home. · It's time I **was going** home.

blocks.text: We can also use a full infinitive after **it's time**, but not after **it's high/about time**.
blocks.note: It's **time to think** about getting a loan.

rows.use: For current, general or future preference
rows.example: Jan would rather/sooner **have bought** a house than **carried** on renting. · Would you rather/sooner I **was begging** in the streets?
We'd rather/sooner you **hadn't lent** Kuldip the money.

blocks.text: **Would rather/sooner** + past simple/continuous is only used to talk about preference regarding someone else. When there is no change of subject, we use **would rather/sooner** + bare infinitive, or **would prefer** + full infinitive.
blocks.note: She'd rather **not borrow** any money from you. · She'd prefer **not to borrow** any money from you.

rows.use: Wishes about now, the future or generally
rows.example: Do you wish you **had** a bigger house? · If only I **was earning** a reasonable salary.
If only I'd **bought** a lottery ticket this morning. · Carla wished she'd **been keeping** a much closer eye on her investments.

blocks.text: When **wish** is in the past simple, it is still followed by the past simple or past continuous for current, future or general wishes.
blocks.note: Simon dearly wished that he **had** a bigger house. · I sat there and wished I **was earning** a reasonable salary.

rows.use: To criticise other people or wish for a situation to be different
rows.example: **wish / if only + would** · I wish they **would** offer me a pay rise.
**wish / if only + could** · I wish I **could** find a job that pays well.

rows.use: Wishes about past ability or permission
rows.example: **wish / if only + could + perfect infinitive** · I wish I **could have got** a mortgage with a fixed interest rate.

rows.use: To express desires in a very formal way
rows.example: **wish + full infinitive** · I wish **to speak** to the bank manager.

rows.use: To wish someone luck, happiness, success, etc.

blocks.text: We do not usually use **would** when the subject of **wish** is the same as the subject of **would**. We do not use **wish** to express desires about a real, possible future. We can use **hope** instead.
blocks.note: Pete wishes he **earned / could earn** more. · I **hope** the cheque arrives tomorrow. (not *I wish the cheque arrives tomorrow.*)

exercises.title: A · The importance of nothing
exercises.instruction: Write the verbs in brackets in the correct form in each gap.

items.prompt: There is a lateral thinking question which asks: 'If the Romans ___ all the technology we have today, why would they not have been able to get to the moon?' (have)
If we ___ to think about this logically, we would probably be unable to come up with a satisfactory reason. (be)
However, with lateral thinking, there is a perfectly reasonable explanation. If the Romans ___ as technologically advanced as we are, they would indeed be stuck here on Earth. (be)
Why? Because if, 2,000 years ago, they ___ a Roman centurion to count down their Roman space rocket, he would have started at ten (in Latin, of course), got down to one and then stopped. (employ)

The Romans had no word for 'zero', so there would have been no 'Lift-off!' Of course, the truth is that if these hypothetical Romans ___ the number 'zero', it would be impossible for them to have all our technology. (have)
If the concept of zero ___ , we would not have computers today. (not / develop)

Modern maths and physics relies absolutely on there being a numeral to represent nothingness. It may seem obvious to us now that zero should exist, but many philosophers in the past were very uncomfortable with the idea. The ancient Greeks tied themselves in logical knots by stating: 'If nothing ___ a number, then it would be something.' (be)
And if it ___ become something, then it would no longer be nothing. (do)
If it ___ for an Indian mathematician called Brahmagupta, who knows what would have happened? (not / be)
He wrote the earliest known text stating that zero was a number. If he ___ , we might not have set foot on the moon either. (not / do)

exercises.title: B · Hypothetical situations
exercises.instruction: Write the verbs in brackets in the correct form in each gap to make hypothetical situations.

items.prompt: Supposing you ___ the chance to spend a year in space, would you take it? (have)
What if we ___ to run away right now and never come back? (decide)
Suppose all your friends ___ bad things about you behind your back and you found out. What would you do? (say)
Imagine you ___ any money or any means of getting any. What on earth could you do? (not / have)
What if the Internet ___ ? Wouldn't that be weird? (not / invent)
Supposing the sun ___ shining right now, how long would it take for us to realise? (stop)
Imagine we ___ that a huge meteor was on its way to Earth. What would be the best thing to do? (just / tell)
Suppose you ___ travel back in time. Where would you go? (can)
What if everyone in the world ___ the same language? (speak)
Suppose it ___ that aliens existed and were living among us! (prove)
I do realise it'll probably never happen but imagine her song ___ really popular! (become)
What if you ___ three wishes by a genie in a bottle? What would you wish for? (give)
Supposing you ___ up one morning and found you'd gone back in time, how would you feel? (wake)
I know we can't travel faster than the speed of light but suppose for a moment that we ___ able to. (be)
Imagine that humans ___ speak. How do you think we'd communicate? (not / can)

exercises.title: C · Which is not correct?
exercises.instruction: Look at the questions that follow each sentence and choose the answer which is not correct.

items.prompt: Why do you always act as if you were better than everyone else, John? Does Rod often act as if he had lots of brothers and sisters? Wait — which follow-up is NOT a possible reading of: 'John better than everyone else'?
items.explanation: as if + past here marks an untrue comparison, so we cannot take it as a fact that he is better.

items.prompt: Rod often acts as if he had lots of brothers and sisters. Does Rod have lots of brothers and sisters?
options: He could have but we don't know.
items.explanation: Past after as if suggests the situation is not (or may not be) true, so a confident 'yes' is not justified.

items.prompt: They look as if they've been running fast. Have they been running fast?
items.explanation: Present perfect after as if marks a possible real situation, so a definite 'no' is the option that does not fit.

items.prompt: There's no need to be frightened of him. Just treat him as if you didn't know he'd spent some time in prison. Do you know about the time he spent in prison?
options: No, you know nothing about it.
acceptedAnswers: No, you know nothing about it.

items.prompt: It was scary! At one point, it felt like we weren't ever going to get out of that jungle alive. How did you feel in the jungle?
options: You would get out of it easily.
You would possibly die in the jungle.
You didn't know if you would survive the jungle or not.
acceptedAnswers: You would get out of it easily.

items.prompt: Sara looked as if she had just woken up. How did Sara look?
options: She looked tired and she wasn't wearing her make-up.
She certainly hadn't just woken up then.
She could possibly just have looked tired but got up a lot earlier.
acceptedAnswers: She certainly hadn't just woken up then.

exercises.title: D · Unreal tenses
exercises.instruction: Write the verbs in brackets in the correct form in each gap. When a situation is hypothetical or unlikely, use unreal tenses.

items.prompt: Dave talks as though he ___ up in the UK, but he actually only moved here three months ago. (grow)
I was such a mess when I got home I looked as if I ___ through a hedge backwards! (drag)
It was such a bad case of flu that I honestly felt as if I ___ to die. (go)
When I saw Corin on TV last night, it felt as if he ___ chat shows for ages. I can't believe this was his first one! (do)
Hardip looked as if he ___ the worst possible news. In fact, he'd failed his finals. (have)
Don't you think Maria sometimes looks as though she ___ she'd been born in another century. (wish)
Rupert often dresses as though he ___ in money but he's actually on the dole. (roll)
You kids are behaving as if it ___ a school night. It is, you know! (not / be)
How can you sit there as if nothing ___ ? (happen)

exercises.title: E · Polite past tenses
exercises.instruction: Make each of these statements or questions as polite as possible by using past tenses. Write the polite version of the missing verbs/phrases.

items.prompt: What time ___ to be woken tomorrow morning? (you, want)
I ___ for an engagement present for a young couple. (look)
acceptedAnswers: wondered if you could help me look

items.prompt: We ___ whether you ___ to go out this evening. (wonder / want)
Excuse me, sir, ___ to park there for long? (you, plan)
___ to see me about something, Mr Patel? (you, wish)
___ for anything in particular? (you, look)
___ milk and sugar in your tea? (you, want)
I ___ you ___ me a hand tomorrow. (hope / give)
How long ___ to stay here? (you, intend)
I ___ if you ___ by credit card, madam. (wonder / pay)

exercises.title: F · it's time
exercises.instruction: Write a verb from the box in the correct form in each gap.

items.prompt: It's high time you ___ smoking. It's a disgusting habit!
It's time you ___ for a job, young man!
I think it's time we ___ a new carpet. This one's got holes in it!
It's time for you kids ___ your homework.

Wake up, Bonnie. It's time ___ now.
Don't you think it's time you ___ a pay rise?
It's time for you ___ a partner in the firm; you've been with them for over eight years, after all.
It's definitely time I ___ to stay out after ten o'clock at night.
It's time for us ___ now, Sammy. Are you ready?
Isn't it about time you ___ to drive?

exercises.title: G · Similar meaning
exercises.instruction: Write a word or short phrase in each gap so that each second sentence has a similar meaning to the first sentence.

items.prompt:
We'd prefer the successful candidate to have previous experience in the field.
We'd rather the successful candidate ___ previous experience in the field.

Would you prefer me to come back later?
Would you rather ___ later?

To be honest, I'd prefer you not to tell anyone about this.
To be honest, I'd rather ___ anyone about this.

I'd prefer us to get a new kitchen rather than go on an expensive holiday.
I'd sooner ___ a new kitchen than go on an expensive holiday.

Dad said he'd prefer Brian to live nearer home and I agree with him.
Dad said he'd rather Brian ___ nearer home and I agree with him.

I would prefer her to be sent on a training course rather than sacked.
I would rather ___ on a training course than sacked.

I'd prefer us not to talk about this right now, if you don't mind.
I'd sooner ___ about this right now, if you don't mind.

Of course I would have preferred you to tell me the truth!
Of course I would rather ___ me the truth!

I think Jeanne would definitely prefer to have a traditional wedding.
I think Jeanne would definitely rather ___ a traditional wedding.

We would have preferred them not to have stayed so long, that's true.
We would sooner ___ so long, that's true.

exercises.title: H · Circle the correct word or phrase
exercises.instruction: Choose the correct option. Where both forms are possible, choose the option that says both.

items.prompt: All of my friends have got mobiles. I wish I ___ one too!
Don't you sometimes wish you ___ this company?

Why on earth does Geoffrey wish he would be given / they would give him a knighthood?
options: he would be given / they would give him
acceptedAnswers: he would be given / they would give him

exercises.title: J · Key word transformation
exercises.instruction: Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. Use between three and eight words, including the word given. Write only the missing part.

items.prompt:
Pauline doesn't want to be given a main part in the school play.
**rather**
Pauline ___ a main part in the school play.

We didn't get to meet the Minister and that was a great shame.
**only**
If ___ to meet the Minister!

Why don't they stop making so much noise downstairs?
**wish**
I ___ making so much noise downstairs!

What a shame I didn't see his face when you told him the news.
**could**
I wish ___ his face when you told him the news.

Don't you think they should bring out a new version of MatchPlayer?
**about**
Don't you think it's ___ out a new version of MatchPlayer?

I only knew about the meeting because Cynthia rang me.
**if**
I wouldn't have known about the meeting ___ me.
